introduction: Asked how many followers He had, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answered that no statistics were kept and that such things were not considered important. The readings that follow measure growth otherwise: by the unity and conduct of the friends, by seeds sown and left to God, by fellowship reaching across East and West, and by a spread that persecution, exile and slander only hastened. They also notice the strain that growth brings and the gratitude it calls for, and they close with later guidance on expansion and consolidation. The New Testament tells a similar story of mustard seed, leaven and a scattered church, and it is quoted throughout, with Isaiah, the Qur’an, Tertullian and Gibbon. The contrasts ask what growth proves and what it costs: Mill and Nietzsche deny that survival or martyrdom shows a cause to be true, Mark Twain remembers missions that travelled with empire, Gandhi asks for respect among religions and not one religion, and the Gospel’s own parables warn of shallow soil and of tares among the wheat.
questions: The first reading declines to count followers, while Acts counts three thousand in a day. What would you want to know about a community before you called it growing?
Several readings say the seed is sown and its growth left to God. What is the sower’s part, and where does it end?

The readings make the unity of the friends the condition of growth, as Jesus prayed that his followers be one so that the world may believe. Why should outsiders be moved by that more than by argument?
Tertullian said the blood of Christians is seed, and Nietzsche that blood is the worst witness to truth. What, on these readings, does persecution show?
Twain saw missions travelling with empire, and Gandhi wanted respect among religions and not one religion. How do the readings describe carrying a message to every land so that it is neither?
Acts records that murmuring arose when the disciples multiplied. What strains would you expect in a community that grows quickly, and what do the last readings advise?

outside.why: Gideon was told that his army was too many, lest Israel say that its own hand had saved it.
The Acts of the Apostles does keep count: three thousand in a day, and others added daily. When are numbers a sign of life, and when a distraction from it?
Jesus named one sign by which his disciples would be known: that they love one another.
James asks his readers to be doers of the word and not hearers only.
Whitman said that he and his kind do not convince by arguments but by their presence.
Malachi foresaw a pure offering made in every place, from the rising of the sun to its going down.
Jesus said that a tree is known by its fruits, and so are those who speak in God's name.
Jesus told his few followers not to fear: it is the Father's good pleasure to give them the kingdom.
Jesus compared the kingdom to a mustard seed, the least of seeds, which becomes a tree where birds lodge.
Zechariah, watching a temple slowly rebuilt, asks who has despised the day of small things.
In the parable of the sower some seed falls on good ground and yields a hundredfold.
Jesus says that the sower sleeps and rises while the seed grows he knows not how: first the blade, then the ear.
Mencius tells of a farmer who pulled at his corn to help it grow, and found it withered. What is the difference between tending a growth and forcing it?
Jesus told his disciples that they reap where others laboured: one sows and another reaps.
Proverbs likens the path of the just to the dawn, shining more and more unto the perfect day.
Carlyle described the century after Muhammad as a spark falling on what proved explosive powder, lighting the world from Delhi to Granada.
Job is told: though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.

Gibbon, no friend of the church, wrote that a pure and humble religion grew up in silence and obscurity and at last set its banner on the ruins of the Capitol. What does a historian's account of such growth explain, and what does it leave unexplained?
Isaiah promises that a little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation.
Jesus said that the coming would be as lightning that comes out of the east and shines even unto the west.
Mark records that in his own country Jesus could do no mighty work, because of their unbelief.
Jesus said of his church that the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
Habakkuk foresaw the earth filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.
The Qur’an says that God sent His messenger with the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religion.
Gamaliel advised the council to leave the apostles alone: if this work be of men it will come to nought, but if of God ye cannot overthrow it.
Mill called it a pleasant falsehood that truth always prevails against persecution: history, he said, teems with truths put down. On what does the confidence of this reading rest?
Jesus prayed that his followers might all be one, so that the world may believe.
Acts says of the first believers that the multitude were of one heart and of one soul.
Joel foresaw the spirit poured out on all flesh, on the servants and on the handmaids alike.
Tertullian reports what the pagans said of the Christians: see how they love one another.
The Dhammapada says that the scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, but the fragrance of the good does.
Paul asks how people shall hear without a preacher, and how any shall preach unless they are sent.
Isaiah says: how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings.
Jesus told his followers to let their light shine before others, so that their good works are seen.
Whitman, writing of canals and railways, saw the oceans crossed and the distant brought near as God's purpose from the first.
Jesus sent his disciples to teach all nations, and promised to be with them always.

Mark Twain, in 1901, called the missions and trading companies that followed the flags of empire the Blessings-of-Civilization Trust. What keeps the carrying of a message to every land from becoming that?
Jesus said that the harvest is plenteous but the labourers are few.
The risen Jesus told the apostles they would be witnesses unto the uttermost part of the earth.
Jesus told his disciples to lift up their eyes and look on the fields, white already to harvest.
Paul speaks of things that eye has not seen, nor ear heard, prepared for those who love God.
The psalm pictures a vine brought out of Egypt that sent out her boughs unto the sea.
The angel told the shepherds: I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
Jesus said that many shall come from the east and west and sit down in the kingdom.
This is the saying the reading recalls: the children of the kingdom shall be cast out.
Paul warned the newly grafted branches not to boast against those broken off. What should those who have entered feel toward those who have not?
Isaiah says that the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
Moses was shown the land from the mountain and did not go over into it.
The elder writes: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Jesus said in his own town that a prophet is not without honour, but in his own country.
David prayed at the offering: Thine, O Lord, is the greatness, and the power, and the victory.
The psalm says that they that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
The crowd at Thessalonica complained of the apostles: these that have turned the world upside down are come hither also.
Marx thought the forces shaking his century were economic: all that is solid melts into air. How would one tell the movement of a Cause from the movement of an age?
Acts says that on the day of Pentecost they were all with one accord in one place when the sound came from heaven.
Kipling wrote that East is East and West is West, and never the twain shall meet, till two strong men stand face to face. What has brought the two together, and what still keeps them apart?
Isaiah says that the grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
Paul told the Corinthians he had fed them with milk and not with meat, for they were not yet able to bear it.
The disciples at Emmaus said: did not our heart burn within us?

Gandhi held that the need of the moment was not one religion but mutual respect among the devotees of different religions. How would he have heard the hope that all communities will come to this Cause?
Daniel saw a stone cut without hands that became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
Ezekiel saw breath come into the slain, and they lived and stood upon their feet.
Kant called it enlightenment to leave the tutelage of inherited authority and use one's own understanding.
Matthew Arnold heard the withdrawal of the old faith as a melancholy roar that left the world without certitude or peace. Is the eclipse of religious imitation glad tidings for everyone?
Shelley's Ozymandias also had renown through the world, and it ended as a boast on a broken pedestal. What kind of fame is worth rejoicing over?
The Qur’an says: when God's succour comes and thou seest mankind entering His religion in troops, then hymn His praises and seek forgiveness.
Isaiah foresaw the word of the Lord going forth from one city to many peoples.
Acts says that a great persecution scattered the church abroad, and those scattered went everywhere preaching.
Tertullian told the persecutors of his day that the oftener Christians are mown down the more they grow: the blood of Christians is seed.
Nietzsche answered that blood is the very worst witness to truth, since every cause has had its martyrs. What besides suffering makes a movement's growth a sign of its truth?
Exodus says of the Israelites in Egypt: the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew.
Paul wrote from prison that what had happened to him had fallen out to the furtherance of the gospel.
Paul wrote in chains: I suffer trouble even unto bonds, but the word of God is not bound.
Jesus called his followers blessed when they are reviled and all manner of evil is said against them falsely.
Paul says that God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the mighty.
Jesus said that a grain of wheat that falls into the ground and dies brings forth much fruit.
After a persecuting king's death Acts adds one line: but the word of God grew and multiplied.
The apostles, beaten, left the council rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame.
Jesus told his disciples that it was expedient for them that he go away.
Proverbs advises: answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
Jesus told his followers to bless those who curse them and pray for those who despitefully use them.
Jeremiah was told: they shall fight against thee, but they shall not prevail against thee.
Jesus said: woe unto you when all men shall speak well of you. What should a community make of favourable attention from newspapers and universities?
The second psalm asks why the rulers take counsel together against the Lord's anointed, and says He shall laugh.
The psalm says that weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning.
Acts records that when the number of disciples was multiplied, a murmuring arose between two groups over the daily distribution.
In the parable the field holds wheat and tares together, and the servants are told to let both grow until the harvest. How should a growing community treat those whose understanding differs?
Moses' father-in-law told him: thou wilt surely wear away; this thing is too heavy for thee alone.
The church at Smyrna is told: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
In the parable some seed springs up quickly on stony ground and withers because it has no root. What does growing prestige need beneath it?
The psalm says: the Lord hath done great things for us, whereof we are glad.
The first letter of Peter calls its readers a chosen people, called out of darkness into marvellous light.
The psalm says: not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto Thy name give glory.
Franklin's almanac has the proverb that God helps them that help themselves. How do confirmation from above and effort from below share in a community's growth?
Moses saw a bush that burned with fire and was not consumed.
Jesus told his disciples that after he went to the Father they would do greater works.
The first letter of Peter asks believers to be ready always to give an answer for the hope that is in them.
Tertullian asked what Athens has to do with Jerusalem, the Academy with the Church. What is gained and what risked when a religion's teachings are correlated with philosophy?
Isaiah gives the two commands in one verse: lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.
The letter to the Ephesians prays that its readers be rooted and grounded in love.

acts-added-to-the-church-daily.text: And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart, Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved

isaiah-little-one-a-thousand.text: A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time

daniel-stone-became-a-mountain.text: Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces. Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them: and the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth

samuel-by-many-or-by-few.text: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few

acts-of-one-heart-and-of-one-soul.text: And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul: neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common

exodus-the-more-they-multiplied.text: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel

acts-murmuring-of-the-grecians.text: And in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration

exodus-thou-wilt-surely-wear-away.text: And Moses' father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone

proverbs-answer-not-a-fool.text: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him

isaiah-lengthen-thy-cords.text: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes; For thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left; and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles, and make the desolate cities to be inhabited

colossians-through-philosophy.text: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ

psalm-not-unto-us.text: Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory, for thy mercy, and for thy truth's sake

psalm-great-things-for-us.text: Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing: then said they among the heathen, The Lord hath done great things for them. The Lord hath done great things for us; whereof we are glad

matthew-harvest-truly-is-plenteous.text: Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest

zechariah-day-of-small-things.text: For who hath despised the day of small things

job-thy-beginning-was-small.text: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase

luke-woe-when-all-speak-well.text: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets

matthew-gates-of-hell.text: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it

acts-word-of-god-grew.text: But the word of God grew and multiplied

psalm-a-vine-out-of-egypt.text: Thou hast brought a vine out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the heathen, and planted it. Thou preparedst room before it, and didst cause it to take deep root, and it filled the land. The hills were covered with the shadow of it, and the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars. She sent out her boughs unto the sea, and her branches unto the river

quran-how-many-a-little-company.text: How many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave! Allah is with the steadfast

quran-prevail-over-all-religion.text: He it is Who hath sent His messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it conqueror of all religion however much idolaters may be averse.
